Explanation: Used to talk about something heard in the past to confirm validity or ask questions, or to make suggestions.
Korean Sentence 1: 안나 씨가 다음 주에 고향에 돌아간다고 하던데 송별회를 준비할까요?
English Sentence 1: I heard that Anna is returning to her hometown next week. Should we prepare a farewell party?
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 정희 씨가 다음 달에 결혼한다고 하던데 정말이에요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 요즘 결혼 준비 때문에 아주 바쁘대요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I heard that Jeonghee is getting married next month. Is that true?
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes, she said she's very busy these days with wedding preparations.

Explanation: Used with action verbs to denote that as soon as an action is taken, something will immediately follow.
Korean Sentence 1: 집에 도착하는대로 연락할게요.
English Sentence 1: I'll call you as soon as I arrive home.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 오늘 언제 집에 올 거니? 빨리 와서 엄마 좀 도와줘.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 수업이 끝나는대로 집에 올게요.
English Sentence 2A: A: When are you coming home today? Come quickly and give Mom a hand.
English Sentence 2B: B: All right. I'll head home as soon as classes are over.

Explanation: Used to acknowledge that the preceding statement is true while implying something else.
Korean Sentence 1: 저는 매운 음식을 먹기는 하지만 좋아하지 않아요.
English Sentence 1: I do eat spicy food, but I don't particularly like it.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 회사 일이 힘들지요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 힘들기는 하지만 배우는 것도 많고 재미있어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Your office work is hard, right?
English Sentence 2B: B: It is hard, but there's so much to learn and it's also fun.

Explanation: Used to express surprise, disbelief, or amazement at something seen or heard.
Korean Sentence 1: 그렇게 건강하던 사람이 병에 걸리다니 믿을 수 없어요.
English Sentence 1: I can't believe that a person so healthy could be sick with a disease.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 내일 서울의 낮 기온이 40도래요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 40도라니 그게 정말이에요?
English Sentence 2A: A: They say it's 40 degrees tomorrow in Seoul.
English Sentence 2B: B: 40 degrees? Is that true?

Explanation: Used to state that something is worth doing or acceptable to carry out.
Korean Sentence 1: 요즘 상영하고 있는 영화 중에서는 '아름다운 꿈'이 볼 만해요.
English Sentence 1: The recent movie "Beautiful Dream" is worth watching.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 한국 음식 중에서 뭐가 제일 맛있어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 불고기가 먹을 만해요. 한번 드셔보세요.
English Sentence 2A: A: What's the best among Korean foods?
English Sentence 2B: B: Bulgogi is worth eating. You should try it out.

Explanation: Used to inform someone about something you think they don't know.
Korean Sentence 1: 제 동생은 노래를 아주 잘 부른답니다.
English Sentence 1: My younger sibling is really good at singing.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 경주는 어떤 곳이에요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 경주는 역사 도시로 유명하답니다.
English Sentence 2A: A: What kind of place is Gyeongju?
English Sentence 2B: B: It's known as the city of history.

Explanation: Used to add additional information to the preceding content.
Korean Sentence 1: 배우 박재성은 연기를 잘할 뿐만 아니라 노래도 잘한대요.
English Sentence 1: Not only is the actor Jaeseong Park good at acting, I heard he's also a good singer.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 슈테판 씨, 한국의 비빔밥은 어떤 음식이에요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 맛있을 뿐만 아니라 영양도 아주 풍부한 음식이에요.
English Sentence 2A: A: What kind of food is bibimbap in Korea, Stephan?
English Sentence 2B: B: Not only is it tasty, it's very nutritious, too.

Explanation: Used to list two or more similar items and connect them to the predicate.
Korean Sentence 1: 제가 과자며 과일이며 음료수까지 다 사 놓았어요.
English Sentence 1: I've already bought everything from cookies to fruit to beverages.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 새로 이사한 하숙집은 어때요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 넓은 방이며 아주머니가 만드신 맛있는 음식이며 마음에 들지 않는 게 없어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: How's the new boarding house?
English Sentence 2B: B: I like everything about it from its spacious room to the delicious food the homeowner makes me.

Explanation: Used to compare two items, stating the preceding item is not as good as the following item.
Korean Sentence 1: 새 노트북이 빠르기는 한데 디자인은 제가 쓰던 노트북만 못해요.
English Sentence 1: The new laptop is fast, but the design doesn't compare to my previous laptop.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 이 영화는 유명한 소설을 영화로 만든 거라면서요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 그런데 영화가 책만 못한 것 같네요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I heard that this movie was based on a famous novel, right?
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes, but the movie isn't half as good as the novel.

Explanation: Used to state that both the preceding and following contents are true or have happened.
Korean Sentence 1: 이 휴대폰은 가볍기도 하고 예쁘기도 해서 인기가 많아요.
English Sentence 1: This cell phone is lightweight and pretty, so it's very popular.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 영하 씨가 쓴 소설이 드라마로 만들어졌다면서요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 다음 주부터 방송이 되는데 기쁘기도 하고 걱정이 되기도 해요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I heard that the novel you wrote was re-made into a drama, Yeongha.
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes, it's going to be aired next week, and I'm both pleased and worried at the same time.

Explanation: Used when making a guess about something that hasn't happened or something unsure about.
Korean Sentence 1: 유키 씨는 바빠서 못 올걸요.
English Sentence 1: I don't think Yuki will be able to come because she's busy.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 레오 씨 전화번호를 아는 사람이 있어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 아마 주앙 씨가 알걸요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Is there anyone who knows Leo's phone number?
English Sentence 2B: B: Juang probably knows it.

Explanation: Used to express that when a situation takes place, another situation will follow, or to make requests.
Korean Sentence 1: 비가 오거나 눈이 내리거나 하면 무서워서 운전을 할 수 없어요.
English Sentence 1: If it rains or snows, I can't drive because I get scared.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 에릭 씨는 미국에 잘 도착했을까요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 문제가 생겼거나 하면 전화를 했겠지요. 걱정하지 마세요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Do you think Eric arrived safely in the U.S.?
English Sentence 2B: B: If something had happened, he would have called. Don't worry.

Explanation: Used to express that the preceding clause is the purpose or cause of the following clause, often with negative results.
Korean Sentence 1: 주말에 아르바이트를 하느라고 쉬지 못했어요.
English Sentence 1: I was working my part-time job over the weekend, so I couldn't rest.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 어제 왜 학교에 안 왔어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 병원에 가느라고 못 왔어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Why weren't you at school yesterday?
English Sentence 2B: B: I had to go to the hospital, so I couldn't make it to school.

Explanation: Used to ask a question to confirm what was said, expressing disbelief or amazement.
Korean Sentence 1: 올가 씨가 한국말을 잘한단 말이에요?
English Sentence 1: You're saying that Olga is good at Korean?
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 제 동생은 5살인데 이번에 피아노 연주회를 해요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 동생이 피아노를 그렇게 잘 친단 말이에요?
English Sentence 2A: A: My younger sibling is 5 years old, but he will be putting on a piano performance this time.
English Sentence 2B: B: You mean to say that your younger brother is that good at piano?

Explanation: Used to state that an action is taken at one location and with its results, another action is taken elsewhere.
Korean Sentence 1: 고향에 갈 때 어머니께 화장품을 사다가 드렸더니 아주 좋아하셨어요.
English Sentence 1: When I went back home, I bought cosmetics and gave it to my mom, and she loved it.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 배고프지? 우리 김밥이라도 사다가 먹을까?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 그래. 떡볶이도 사다가 먹자.
English Sentence 2A: A: Are you hungry? How about we buy some gimbap to eat?
English Sentence 2B: B: All right. Let's also buy some tteokbokki to eat.

Explanation: Used to express disbelief or amazement at something someone has said, or to negate their statement.
Korean Sentence 1: 미선 씨가 김치를 싫어하다니요? 잘 먹던데요.
English Sentence 1: What do you mean Miseon doesn't like kimchi? She ate it really well.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 일요일 파티에 왜 안 왔어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 파티에 안 가다니요? 그날 제가 앞에 나가서 노래도 불렀잖아요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Why didn't you come to the party on Sunday?
English Sentence 2B: B: What do you mean, not go? I was sitting at the front and even sang a song that day.

Explanation: Used to make a speculation based on something seen or observed.
Korean Sentence 1: 누리가 계속 전화를 안 받는 걸 보니 오늘 정말 바쁜가 봐요.
English Sentence 1: Seeing that she is not answering the phone, she must be really busy today.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 우리 뭐 먹을까? 어느 식당이 유명한지 잘 모르겠네.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 사람들이 길게 줄을 선 걸 보니 저 식당 음식이 맛있나 봐. 우리도 저기에 가자.
English Sentence 2A: A: What should we eat? I don't know which restaurant is famous.
English Sentence 2B: B: Seeing as though there's a long line of people, that restaurant must have good food. Let's go there.

Explanation: Used to state that something ends when a final action is taken.
Korean Sentence 1: 명절 선물은 다 준비했으니까 이제 보내기만 하면 됩니다.
English Sentence 1: I've already prepared the holiday gift, so all I need to do is send it.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 찌개 끓일 재료는 다 준비해 놓았니?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 네, 재료를 썰어서 냄비에 담고 양념도 넣었어요. 이제 끓이기만 하면 돼요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Have you prepared all the ingredients to cook the stew?
English Sentence 2B: B: Yes. I've chopped up the ingredients, placed them in a pot, and I've even added the seasoning. All that's left is to bring it to a boil.

Explanation: Used to state that a repetitive action was taken during a set period of time.
Korean Sentence 1: 주말에 할 일이 없으면 혼자 영화를 보러 가곤 해요.
English Sentence 1: I go to watch movies by myself when I have nothing to do on the weekends.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 우리 오늘 점심은 신촌역 앞에 있는 행복식당에서 먹을까?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 좋아. 대학생 때 거기에서 자주 먹곤 했는데. 그때가 생각난다.
English Sentence 2A: A: Why don't we eat at Haengbok restaurant near Sinchon Station for lunch tomorrow?
English Sentence 2B: B: Sure. I used to eat there often in college. I remember those days.

Explanation: Used to emphasize the following clause regardless of the situation, comparing two relative concepts.
Korean Sentence 1: 잘하건 못하건 끝까지 하는 게 중요하지요.
English Sentence 1: Whether you're good at it or not, it's important that you keep at it until the end.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 저는 이번 달 모임에 가지 못할 것 같은데 회비를 안 내도 되겠지요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 모임에 가건 안 가건 회비는 꼭 내야 한대요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I don't think I'll be able to make it to this month's meeting. I don't have to pay the membership fee, right?
English Sentence 2B: B: Whether you go to the meeting or not, you need to pay the membership fee.

Explanation: Used to state that while an action was taking place, another action took place.
Korean Sentence 1: 제가 잠깐 마트에 다녀오는 사이에 도둑이 집에 있던 돈을 가지고 갔어요.
English Sentence 1: While I was at the store, a thief came into the house and stole all my money.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 어떻게 강아지를 잃어버리셨어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 제가 공원에서 이웃을 만나서 잠깐 이야기하는 사이에 강아지가 없어졌어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: How did you lose your puppy?
English Sentence 2B: B: I met a neighbor in the park and while we were sharing a short conversation, my puppy disappeared.

Explanation: Used to pretend to do something not actually done or state something untrue.
Korean Sentence 1: 비밀을 알고 있으면서도 모르는 척했어요.
English Sentence 1: I knew the secret, but pretended as though I didn't.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 왜 엄마한테 혼났어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 공부하는 척하면서 만화책을 봤거든요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Why did you get in trouble by your mom?
English Sentence 2B: B: Because I pretended to be studying while reading a comic book.

Explanation: Used to make a proposal or recommendation.
Korean Sentence 1: 안느 씨, 그렇게 아프면 약이라도 먹지 그래요?
English Sentence 1: Anne, why don't you take some medicine if you're that sick?
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 동아리 모임 장소를 정해야 하는데 쉽지 않네요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 교회 앞에 새로 생긴 '미소'에서 하지 그래요? 넓은 방이 있어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I'm trying to decide on a location for our club meeting, but it's not easy.
English Sentence 2B: B: How about that newly opened place "Miso" in front of the church? It has some large rooms.

Explanation: Used to make requests, give instructions, or make promises given certain conditions are met.
Korean Sentence 1: 동아리 행사가 끝나거든 모두 모임 장소로 오세요.
English Sentence 1: Once the club activity ends, come to the meeting location.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 엄마, 너무 걱정하지 마세요. 가서 열심히 할게요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 그래, 공항에 도착하거든 바로 전화부터 해라.
English Sentence 2A: A: Mom, don't worry so much. I'll go and do my best.
English Sentence 2B: B: All right. Once you arrive at the airport, give me a call.

Explanation: Used when unsure about a judgment that has been made.
Korean Sentence 1: 동생이 이 선물을 좋아할지 모르겠어요.
English Sentence 1: I'm not sure if my younger sibling will like this gift.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 영수 씨, 우리 1시간 일찍 출발했으니까 회의 시간에 늦지는 않겠죠?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 글쎄요. 길이 많이 막혀서 제시간에 도착할지 모르겠네요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Yeongsu, we left an hour early, so we probably won't be late to the meeting, right?
English Sentence 2B: B: I don't know. I'm not sure we'll arrive on time since there's so much traffic.

Explanation: Used to show the preceding clause is one of many reasons for the following content.
Korean Sentence 1: 어제는 비도 오고 해서 하루종일 집에만 있었어요.
English Sentence 1: It rained yesterday, so I just stayed at home all day.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 왜 '우정 커피숍'에 자주 가요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 분위기도 좋고 해서 자주 가요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Why do you go so often to "Friendship Coffee Shop"?
English Sentence 2B: B: The atmosphere is nice so I go there often.

Explanation: Used to express regret over what someone else did not do that was opposite to what was wanted.
Korean Sentence 1: 내가 전에 이야기했을 때 병원에 가지.
English Sentence 1: You should've gone to the hospital when I told you to.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 어제 '너와 함께'라는 영화를 봤는데 진짜 재미있었어.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 보고 싶었던 영화인데 나도 좀 데리고 가지.
English Sentence 2A: A: I watched the movie "With you" yesterday and it was so fun.
English Sentence 2B: B: I wanted to watch it, too. You should've taken me with you.

Explanation: Used to strongly emphasize speculation, expressing concern, regret, or making proposals.
Korean Sentence 1: 승환 씨는 독서를 좋아하니까 책을 선물하면 좋아할 텐데요.
English Sentence 1: Seunghwan likes to read, so it'd be nice to give him a book as a gift.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 미영 씨에게도 내일 같이 등산을 하자고 말해볼까요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 미영 씨는 보통 주말에 부모님 댁에 가니까 시간이 안 될 텐데요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Should we ask Miyeong if she wants to go hiking tomorrow?
English Sentence 2B: B: Miyeong probably won't have time since she usually goes to see her parents on the weekends.

Explanation: Used when an action is taken based on information heard or seen.
Korean Sentence 1: 성적이 좋으면 장학금을 준다고 해서 열심히 공부하고 있어요.
English Sentence 1: I heard that scholarships will be given for good grades, so I'm studying hard.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 이번 휴가 때는 어디로 여행을 갈 거예요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 경주에 역사 유적이 많다고 해서 경주에 갈까 해요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Where are you going to do during the vacation?
English Sentence 2B: B: I heard that there are many historical sites in Gyeongju, so I'm considering vacationing in Gyeongju.

Explanation: Used to state that an unintentional situation resulted from carrying out an action.
Korean Sentence 1: 백화점에 갔다가 초등학교 동창을 만났어요.
English Sentence 1: I went to the department store and happened to meet my elementary school classmate.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 어떻게 리나 씨랑 같이 와요? 같은 하숙집에 살아요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 아니요, 편의점에 들렀다가 리나 씨를 만났어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: How are you two coming together? Do you live in the same boarding house as Lina?
English Sentence 2B: B: No, I stopped by the convenience store and happened to meet Lina there.

Explanation: Used when supposing something that didn't happen in the past happened, or vice versa.
Korean Sentence 1: 존이 도와주지 않았다면 이 일을 다 끝내지 못했을 거예요.
English Sentence 1: If John hadn't helped us, we wouldn't have been able to finish this.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 오늘 경기 결과가 대단한데요. 한 말씀 부탁드립니다.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 저 혼자 했다면 이런 결과는 없었을 겁니다. 도와주신 분들께 감사드립니다.
English Sentence 2A: A: Today's match results are amazing. May I ask for your remarks?
English Sentence 2B: B: If I were playing alone, this kind of result could not have been achieve. I'd like to thank everyone for their help.

Explanation: Used to express there is a slight possibility of something happening.
Korean Sentence 1: 금요일로 약속을 정하면 노리코 씨가 못 올 수도 있잖아요.
English Sentence 1: If we set the date for Friday, Noriko may not be able to make it.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 에릭 씨, 7시쯤 회사 앞에서 기다릴까요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 좀 늦을 수도 있으니까 제가 다시 연락드릴게요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Eric, should I wait in front of the company around 7 p.m.?
English Sentence 2B: B: I may be late, so let me give you a call.

Explanation: Used to show the preceding content is the tool, means, method, ingredient, or object of the following clause.
Korean Sentence 1: 버리는 종이를 가지고 옷을 만들었어요.
English Sentence 1: I made clothes out of paper scraps.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 한국말을 잘하니까 한국 회사에 지원해보세요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 이 정도 실력을 가지고 한국 회사에서 일할 수 있을까요?
English Sentence 2A: A: You should apply for a position at a Korean company since you're good at Korean.
English Sentence 2B: B: Can I work at a Korean company with this level of Korean?

Explanation: Used to express past contents different from present, or temporary past actions.
Korean Sentence 1: 작년 여름에 제주도에 갔었어요.
English Sentence 1: I went to Jeju Island last summer.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 이번 주말에 여자친구와 놀이공원에 가려고 해요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 저도 지난 주말에 갔었는데 날씨가 좋아서 놀기 좋았어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: I'm planning to go to the amusement park with my girlfriend this weekend.
English Sentence 2B: B: I went last weekend, and the weather was so nice and perfect for playing.

Explanation: Used to express a choice that is more of an alternative rather than fully satisfactory.
Korean Sentence 1: 나는 집에 가서 숙제나 해야겠다.
English Sentence 1: I should just go home and do my homework.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 주디야, 시험도 끝났는데 넌 오늘 뭐 할 거야?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 집에 가서 잠이나 자려고. 시험 때문에 긴장해서 그런지 너무 피곤해.
English Sentence 2A: A: Judy, what are you doing today, now that exams are over?
English Sentence 2B: B: I'm just going to go home and take a nap. Maybe it's because I was so nervous about the tests, but I'm exhausted.

Explanation: Used to show that with progressive advancement, the degree of the following clause also changes.
Korean Sentence 1: 한국말은 배울수록 재미있어요.
English Sentence 1: The more I study Korean, the more fun it is.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 패티 씨, 기분은 어때요? 좀 괜찮아졌어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 아니요. 생각할수록 화가 나요.
English Sentence 2A: A: Patty, how are you feeling? Are you better now?
English Sentence 2B: B: No. The more I think about it, the angrier I feel.

Explanation: Used to express that an action has been completed with nothing remaining, often with wistful or relieved feelings.
Korean Sentence 1: 스타일을 바꾸고 싶어서 머리를 짧게 잘라버렸어요.
English Sentence 1: I wanted to change my style, so I ended up cutting my hair short.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 어제 미선 씨하고 영화를 본다고 했잖아요. 재미있었어요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 아니요, 미선 씨가 갑자기 집에 가버려서 영화를 못 봤어요.
English Sentence 2A: A: You said you were going to watch a movie with Miseon yesterday. Was it fun?
English Sentence 2B: B: No, Miseon suddenly ended up going home, so we couldn't watch the movie.

Explanation: Used to speculate about something based on what's seen or heard.
Korean Sentence 1: 실력이 점점 좋아지는 걸 보면 요즘 연습을 열심히 하는 모양이에요.
English Sentence 1: It seems like you're practicing very hard these days, seeing as though your skills are progressively improving.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 출발할 시간이 다 됐는데 왜 안 올까요? 연락해보세요.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 에디 씨가 좀 늦을 모양이에요.
English Sentence 2A: A: It's time to leave. Why isn't he coming? Give him a call.
English Sentence 2B: B: It seems Eddie is running a bit late.

Explanation: Used when assuming something has been completed or considering opposite results for ongoing actions.
Korean Sentence 1: 민수는 오늘 회사에서 회식이 있다고 했으니까 저녁을 먹었을 텐데요.
English Sentence 1: Minsu said he had a company dinner today, so he probably already ate dinner.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 우산이 없으면 미리 연락을 하지. 그랬으면 데리러 갔을 텐데.
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 가까운 거리니까 괜찮을 거라고 생각했어.
English Sentence 2A: A: You should've called sooner if you didn't have an umbrella. Then, I would've gone to pick you up.
English Sentence 2B: B: I thought it would be all right since it's so close by.

Explanation: Used to express the size or degree of a person or product being compared.
Korean Sentence 1: 우리 형은 키가 저만해요.
English Sentence 1: My older brother is as tall as me.
Korean Sentence 2A: 가: 제임스 씨 고향은 얼마나 커요?
Korean Sentence 2B: 나: 우리 고향은 서울만한 것 같아요. 그렇게 크지 않아요.
English Sentence 2A: A: James, how big is your hometown?
English Sentence 2B: B: My hometown is about as big as Seoul, I believe. It's not that big.
